Furthermore, one is an alms-round practitioner solely depending on fewness of wishes (appicchatā), solely depending on contentment (santuṭṭhi), solely depending on effacement (sallekha), and solely depending on the value of this practice itself (idamatthisatā). Among these alms-round practitioners, the one who is an alms-round practitioner solely depending on fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, and the value of this practice itself is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent of these five alms-round practitioners.

Just as from a cow comes milk, from milk curds, from curds butter, from butter ghee, and from ghee the cream of ghee, and the cream of ghee is said to be the best of them; even so, the alms-round practitioner who is an alms-round practitioner solely depending on fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, and the value of this practice itself is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent of these five alms-round practitioners. These are the five types of alms-round practitioners.
180:
In that (Exposition of the Fives), what are the five types of persons who are khalupacchābhattika (one who refuses later food)? ...pe... the five types of ekāsanika (one who eats in one sitting), ...pe... the five types of paṃsukūlika (refuse-rag wearer), ...pe... the five types of tecīvarika (three-robe wearer), ...pe... the five types of āraññika (forest dweller), ...pe... the five types of rukkhamūlika (tree-root dweller), ...pe... the five types of abbhokāsika (open-air dweller), ...pe... the five types of nesajjika (sitter), ...pe... the five types of yathāsanthatika (one who accepts whatever seat is offered).

In that (Exposition of the Fives), what are the five types of sosānika (cemetery dweller)? One is a cemetery dweller because of dullness and delusion; one is a cemetery dweller because of evil desires and being overwhelmed by longing; one is a cemetery dweller because of insanity and mental distraction; one is a cemetery dweller thinking, 'This is praised by the Buddha and the Buddha's disciples'; and furthermore, one is a cemetery dweller based only on fewness of wishes (appicchatā), based only on contentment (santuṭṭhi), based only on effacement (sallekha), and based only on the worthiness of the practice (idamaṭṭhitā). Among these cemetery dwellers, the one who is a cemetery dweller based only on fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, and the worthiness of the practice is the chief, the best, the foremost, the highest, and the most excellent among these five types of cemetery dwellers.

Just as from a cow comes milk, from milk comes curd, from curd comes fresh butter, from fresh butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes the cream of ghee, and that cream of ghee is reckoned the best; even so, the cemetery dweller who is so based only on fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, and the worthiness of the practice is the chief, the best, the foremost, the highest, and the most excellent among these five types of cemetery dwellers. These are the five types of cemetery dwellers.

## The Exposition of the Fives is finished.

## 6. Chakkapuggalapaññatti (Designation of Six Persons)

In that (Designation of Six Persons), here a certain person, in regard to truths unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself, and in those truths, he attains omniscience and mastery over the powers (balas). Such a person is to be understood as a Sammāsambuddha (Fully Enlightened Buddha).

In that (Designation of Six Persons), here a certain person, in regard to truths unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself, but in those truths, he does not attain omniscience nor mastery over the powers. Such a person is to be understood as a Paccekasambuddha (Solitary Buddha).
181:
Among those persons, here a certain person, in regard to truths unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself, becomes one who makes an end of suffering in this very life, and attains the perfection of a disciple (sāvakapāramī). Such a person is to be understood like the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Moggallāna.

Among those persons, here a certain person, in regard to truths unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself, becomes one who makes an end of suffering in this very life, but does not attain the perfection of a disciple. Such a person is to be understood like the remaining Arahants.

Among those persons, here a certain person, in regard to truths unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself, but does not make an end of suffering in this very life; he becomes an Anāgāmī (Non-returner) who does not return to this state of existence. Such a person is to be understood as an Anāgāmī person.

Among those persons, here a certain person, in regard to truths unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself, but does not make an end of suffering in this very life; he is one who must return to this state of existence. Such a person is to be understood as the Sotāpanna (Stream-enterer) and Sakadāgāmī (Once-returner) persons.

## The Exposition of the Sixes is finished.

## 7. Sattakapuggalapaññatti (Designation of Seven Persons)

How is a person one who, having once sunk, remains sunk? Here, a certain person is possessed of absolutely dark, unwholesome states. Thus, a person, having once sunk, remains sunk.

How is a person one who, having emerged, sinks again? Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: 'Faith (saddhā) in wholesome states is good, shame (hirī) in wholesome states is good, moral dread (ottappa) in wholesome states is good, energy (vīriya) in wholesome states is good, wisdom (paññā) in wholesome states is good.' But that faith of his neither stays nor grows, but only declines. That shame of his neither stays nor grows, but only declines. That moral dread of his neither stays nor grows, but only declines. That energy of his neither stays nor grows, but only declines. That wisdom of his neither stays nor grows, but only declines. Thus, a person, having emerged, sinks again.
182:
And how does a person, having emerged, stand still? Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: 'Faith in wholesome states is good, shame in wholesome states is good, fear of wrongdoing in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good.' That faith of his neither decreases nor increases, but stands still. That shame of his neither decreases nor increases, but stands still. That fear of wrongdoing of his neither decreases nor increases, but stands still. That energy of his neither decreases nor increases, but stands still. That wisdom of his neither decreases nor increases, but stands still. In this way, a person, having emerged, stands still.

And how does a person, having emerged, see and observe with insight? Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: 'Faith in wholesome states is good, shame in wholesome states is good, fear of wrongdoing in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good.' With the destruction of the three fetters, he becomes a stream-enterer (sotāpanna), no longer subject to rebirth in lower worlds, fixed in destiny, with enlightenment as his destination. In this way, a person, having emerged, sees and observes with insight.

And how does a person, having emerged, swim? Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: 'Faith in wholesome states is good, shame in wholesome states is good, fear of wrongdoing in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good.' With the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, he becomes a once-returner (sakadāgāmī), who, returning to this world only once more, makes an end of suffering. In this way, a person, having emerged, swims.

And how does a person, having emerged, reach a foothold? Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: 'Faith in wholesome states is good, shame in wholesome states is good, fear of wrongdoing in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good.' With the destruction of the five lower fetters, he is of spontaneous birth (opapātika), attaining final Nibbāna there, not liable to return from that world. In this way, a person, having emerged, reaches a foothold.

And how does a person, having emerged, become one who has crossed over, reached the far shore, stands on dry land, a Brahmin who has discarded evil? Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: 'Faith in wholesome states is good...
183:
...shame in wholesome states is good, fear of wrongdoing in wholesome states is good, energy in wholesome states is good, wisdom in wholesome states is good. With the destruction of the taints (āsavas), he enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, having realized them for himself by direct knowledge in this very life. In this way, a person, having emerged, is one who has crossed over, reached the far shore, stands on the dry land of Nibbāna, a Brahmin who has put away evil.

And what kind of person is liberated in both ways (ubhatobhāgavimutta)? Here, a certain person dwells having touched the eight liberations (vimokkhas) with his mental body, and his taints are destroyed by his seeing with wisdom. This person is called liberated in both ways.

And what kind of person is liberated by wisdom (paññāvimutta)... (and so on) the body-witness (kāyasakkhī)... one attained to vision (diṭṭhippatta)... one liberated by faith (saddhāvimutta)... a Dhamma-follower (dhammānusārī)...

And what kind of person is a faith-follower (saddhānusārī)? For a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the faculty of faith is predominant; he develops the noble path led by faith, preceded by faith. This person is called a faith-follower. A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is a faith-follower; one established in the fruit is one liberated by faith.

## Exposition of the Sevens.

## 8. Designation of Persons by Eights

In that group, who are the four persons possessed of the path and the four persons possessed of the fruit? The stream-enterer (sotāpanna), the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry; the once-returner (sakadāgāmī), the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning; the non-returner (anāgāmī), the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning; the arahant, the one practicing for the realization of the fruit of arahantship. These four are the persons possessed of the path, and these four are the persons possessed of the fruit.

## Exposition of the Eights.
184:
## 9. Designation of Groups of Nine

What kind of person is a Fully Enlightened Buddha (Sammāsambuddha)? Here, a certain person, in regard to things unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself and attains omniscience therein, as well as mastery over the five powers. This person is called a Fully Enlightened Buddha.

What kind of person is a Paccekabuddha? Here, a certain person, in regard to things unheard of before, realizes the Four Noble Truths by himself, but does not attain omniscience therein, nor mastery over the five powers. This person is called a Paccekabuddha.

What kind of person is one liberated in both ways (Ubhatobhāgavimutta)? Here, a certain person dwells having touched the eight liberations (vimokkha) with the mental body, and his taints (āsava) are destroyed by seeing with wisdom. This person is called one liberated in both ways.

What kind of person is one liberated by wisdom (Paññāvimutta)? Here, a certain person does not dwell having touched the eight liberations with the mental body, but his taints are destroyed by seeing with wisdom. This person is called one liberated by wisdom.

What kind of person is a body-witness (Kāyasakkhī)? Here, a certain person dwells having touched the eight liberations with the mental body, and some of his taints are destroyed by seeing with wisdom. This person is called a body-witness.

What kind of person is one attained to vision (Diṭṭhippatta)? Here, a certain person understands as it really is: 'This is suffering'... (pe) ...understands as it really is: 'This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering.' The teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are well seen and well practiced by him through wisdom, and some of his taints are destroyed by seeing with wisdom. This person is called one attained to vision.

What kind of person is one liberated by faith (Saddhāvimutta)? Here, a certain person understands as it really is: 'This is suffering'... (pe) ...understands as it really is: 'This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering.' The teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are [well seen and well practiced] by him through wisdom...
185:
...well seen and well practiced; and some of his taints are destroyed by seeing with wisdom, but not to the same extent as one attained to vision (in terms of wisdom). This person is called one liberated by faith.

What kind of person is a Dhamma-follower (Dhammānusārī)? For a certain person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry (sotāpattiphala), the faculty of wisdom (paññindriya) is predominant; he develops the noble path led by wisdom. This person is called a Dhamma-follower. A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is a Dhamma-follower; one established in the fruit is one attained to vision.

What kind of person is a faith-follower (Saddhānusārī)? For a certain person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the faculty of faith (saddhindriya) is predominant; he develops the noble path led by faith. This person is called a faith-follower. A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is a faith-follower; one established in the fruit is one liberated by faith.

## Exposition of the Nines.

## 10. Designation of Groups of Ten

Which five persons reach their end here (in the sense-sphere)? The one who will be reborn seven times at most (Sattakkhattuparama), the one who goes from family to family (Kolaṅkola), the one-seeder (Ekabījī), the once-returner (Sakadāgāmī), and the one who is an Arahant in this very life. These five persons reach their end here.

Which five persons reach their end after leaving here? The one who attains Nibbāna in the interval (Antarāparinibbāyī), the one who attains Nibbāna after landing (Upahaccaparinibbāyī), the one who attains Nibbāna without exertion (Asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī), the one who attains Nibbāna with exertion (Sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī), and the one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm (Uddhaṃsota-akaniṭṭhagāmī). These five persons reach their end after leaving here.

With this much, the designation of individuals is completed.

## Exposition of the Tens.
